prompt.context: Our client, Veratech, is an international tech firm that sells hardware and additional add-on services. Recently, its market share in the US has been falling and it has hired us to determine how to regain market share.
prompt.question: What is causing Veratech's market share to fall in the US, and what should Veratech do to regain it?

clarifying_info.q: Are we focused on the US market or globally?
clarifying_info.a: We will focus on the US market.

clarifying_info.q: What does Veratech's revenue breakdown look like?
clarifying_info.a: Revenue is split 50/50 between Hardware and Services, and 70/30 between B2B and B2C.

clarifying_info.q: How is Veratech positioned on price?
clarifying_info.a: Veratech is a high-end, premium-priced provider offering customized solutions.
There are 5 competitors outside of Veratech that make up the entirety of the market.

clarifying_info.q: Have the customer base or customer preferences changed?
clarifying_info.a: Customers have not changed year over year.

clarifying_info.q: How does Veratech compare to competitors in terms of product positioning?
clarifying_info.a: Competitor C offers a mass-market hardware/services product while Veratech offers a customized high-end product.

exhibits.title: Market Analysis
exhibits.shows: A market analysis summary with three sections: Competition (market share last year vs. this year for each player), Market (total market size, segment sizes, and growth rates), and Costs (B2B cost trend and reason).
exhibits.data: Competition — A: 10%→10%, B: 10%→10%, C: 20%→25%, D: 20%→20%, E: 20%→20%, Veratech: 20%→15%. Market — Total: $1B; Mass market: $750M; High-end: $250M; Total growth: 4%; Mass market growth: 5%; High-end growth: 1%. Costs — B2B segment costs up 20%; reason: customer service hours are up.

exhibits.title: Competitor Market Share Chart
exhibits.shows: A visual chart displaying the market share positions or breakdown of competitors in the market (exact chart type visible in image).
exhibits.data: See image for visual representation of competitor market share data.

framework: Current Customers / Current Products: offer volume discounts, institute loyalty programs, utilize long-term contracts
Current Customers / New Products: R&D for new products, complementary services
New Customers / Current Products: lower prices, increase B2C presence, increase advertising
New Customers / New Products: expand to new markets/segments, increase advertising, R&D for new products, institute partnerships

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 1. What does this tell you, and what recommendations would you make for Veratech based on this data?
questions.guidance: Strong answer covers: (1) Market is growing (4%) but slowly; mass market ($750M, 5% growth) is far larger and growing faster than high-end ($250M, 1% growth). (2) Veratech is the only player losing share (20%→15%); Competitor C is the only one gaining share (20%→25%) — this is a Veratech-specific problem, not an industry-wide decline. (3) B2B costs are rising 20% due to increased customer service hours. (4) Conclusion: the high-end segment is shrinking in relative terms; customers are gravitating toward mass-market solutions offered by Competitor C. Veratech should consider entering the mass-market segment via: developing new products in-house, acquiring a competitor, or forming partnerships.

questions.prompt: Look at Exhibit 2. Does this information change your recommendation? What risks do you see for Veratech in entering the mass-market segment?
questions.guidance: Recommendation should not change, but candidate must acknowledge Veratech faces considerable established competition in mass-market (especially Competitor C). Candidate should also note hedging by maintaining high-end share in case mass-market penetration is slow. Key risks and options to discuss: (1) Enter mass market — Risk: competitors already established; Risk: diluting the high-end customized brand with a commoditized product. (2) Lower price of existing products — Risk: hurts the 'high-end' image of Veratech's existing offerings. (3) Shift focus from B2B to B2C — Costs are rising in B2B; shifting to B2C could reach more customers without raising costs — Risk: reaching B2C clients is harder and may require additional investment in sales.

recommendation: Adopt a 2-tier pricing model: offer both customized high-end products and a new mass-market product line, with particular emphasis on the B2C segment where costs are more stable
Start developing a mass-market product to capture the faster-growing $750M segment where Competitor C has been gaining share
Cut customer service costs in B2B to lower the price point on current products and address the 20% cost increase
risks: Competition: the mass-market segment has several established competitors, especially Competitor C, which already has momentum
Timing: Competitor C could continue taking market share while Veratech develops a mass-market solution
Brand/employee buy-in: Veratech's employees and customers associate the brand with being the high-end provider; entering mass market risks diluting that identity
next_steps: Begin R&D or M&A process to develop or acquire a mass-market hardware/services offering
Analyze and reduce customer service costs driving the B2B cost increase (e.g., improved self-service tools, tiered support)
Evaluate B2C channel investment required to shift the 70/30 B2B-B2C revenue mix and assess ROI
